title: Healthy Habits
target_phrases: I need to cut down on...

dialogue.title: Discussing Fitness and Nutrition
dialogue.context: Ahmed and coworkers talk about their health routines during lunch break.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: You guys always seem so energetic. Do you exercise regularly?

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: I try to! I go to the gym three times a week - Monday, Wednesday, and Friday mornings before work.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: I play soccer every Saturday and Sunday. It's fun and great exercise at the same time.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: I should exercise more. I'm always too tired after work.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: That's why I go in the morning! If I wait until evening, I make excuses. What about your diet? Do you cook at home?

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Not as much as I should. I eat a lot of fast food because it's convenient. I know it's not healthy.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: I meal prep on Sundays. I cook healthy meals for the whole week and freeze them. It saves time and money.

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: That's smart! Also, Ahmed, are you getting enough sleep? Sleep is just as important as exercise and diet.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: Honestly, no. I usually sleep only 5-6 hours. I stay up late watching TV.

lines.speaker: Carlos
lines.text: You should aim for 7-8 hours. Your body needs rest to stay healthy and have energy.

lines.speaker: Ahmed
lines.text: You're right. My goal is to eat healthier, exercise more, and sleep better. Maybe we can be workout partners?

lines.speaker: Lisa
lines.text: Absolutely! Let's start this weekend. Small changes make a big difference over time.

listening_exercises.transcript: A balanced diet includes five food groups: fruits, vegetables, grains, proteins, and dairy. Try to fill half your plate with fruits and vegetables. Choose whole grains like brown rice and whole wheat bread over white rice and white bread. Include lean proteins like chicken, fish, beans, and nuts. Limit processed foods, sugar, and salt.
listening_exercises.question: What should fill half your plate?

listening_exercises.transcript: The CDC recommends adults get at least 150 minutes of moderate exercise per week. That's about 30 minutes, five days a week. Moderate exercise includes brisk walking, swimming, or bike riding. You don't need a gym membership - walking is free and very beneficial. Even breaking it into three 10-minute walks throughout the day works.
listening_exercises.question: How much exercise do adults need per week?

listening_exercises.transcript: Sleep is crucial for health. Adults need 7-9 hours per night. Lack of sleep affects your immune system, weight, mood, and concentration. Create good sleep habits: go to bed at the same time, avoid screens an hour before bed, keep your bedroom cool and dark, and don't eat heavy meals late at night.
listening_exercises.question: How many hours of sleep do adults need?

speaking_tasks.prompt: Describe your weekly exercise routine OR a routine you want to start. Include how often and what type of exercise. Record for 30 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: I'm trying to develop a better exercise routine. Right now, I walk for 20 minutes three times a week during my lunch break. I want to increase this to 30 minutes, five days a week. I also want to add some strength training - maybe using free weights or doing push-ups and sit-ups at home. My goal is to feel more energetic and strong. I know I need to start slow and build up gradually to avoid injury.

speaking_tasks.prompt: Give advice to someone who wants to eat healthier but doesn't have much time. Suggest 3 tips. Record for 25 seconds.
speaking_tasks.example: If you want to eat healthier but you're busy, here are three tips. First, meal prep on weekends - cook healthy meals and freeze them for the week. Second, keep healthy snacks available like fruits, nuts, and yogurt so you don't reach for junk food. Third, drink a lot of water throughout the day instead of soda or juice. These small changes are easy to maintain and will make a big difference in your health.

writing_tasks.prompt: Write about your current health habits. What do you do well? What do you want to improve? (60-80 words)
writing_tasks.example: I think I have some good health habits, but I could improve in other areas. I drink a lot of water every day, which is good. I also try to eat fruits and vegetables with most meals. However, I need to exercise more regularly - right now I only walk occasionally. I also need to sleep more. I often stay up late on my phone and only get 6 hours of sleep. My goal is to exercise at least three times a week and sleep 8 hours every night.

writing_tasks.prompt: Create a simple meal plan for one day. Include breakfast, lunch, dinner, and snacks. Make it healthy and balanced. (50-70 words)
writing_tasks.example: Here's my healthy meal plan for one day: Breakfast - oatmeal with berries and a banana. Mid-morning snack - apple with peanut butter. Lunch - grilled chicken salad with vegetables and olive oil dressing. Afternoon snack - carrots and hummus. Dinner - baked salmon, brown rice, and steamed broccoli. This plan includes all food groups, lots of vegetables, lean protein, and whole grains. I would drink water throughout the day.

grammar_focus.title: Frequency Adverbs (always, usually, sometimes, rarely, never)
grammar_focus.explanation: Use frequency adverbs to describe how often you do healthy activities. They usually come before the main verb.
examples: I always eat breakfast. (100% of the time)
She usually exercises in the morning. (most of the time)
He sometimes eats fast food. (occasionally)
We rarely drink soda. (not often)
They never skip meals. (0% of the time)

grammar_focus.title: 'Should' for Health Recommendations
grammar_focus.explanation: Use 'should' to give advice or recommendations about health.
examples: You should exercise regularly. (recommendation)
I should eat more vegetables. (what I need to do)
We should get 8 hours of sleep. (advice)
She should drink more water. (recommendation)

grammar_focus.title: Present Simple for Habits
grammar_focus.explanation: Use present simple to talk about regular habits and routines.
examples: I exercise every morning. (habit)
She eats salad for lunch. (routine)
He drinks water all day. (habit)
They sleep 8 hours. (routine)

cultural_notes: The U.S. has high rates of obesity - about 40% of adults. Fast food and processed foods are major contributing factors.
Gyms are popular in the U.S. Common chains include Planet Fitness, LA Fitness, and 24 Hour Fitness.
Many Americans track fitness with apps and wearable devices like Fitbit or Apple Watch.
Meal prep on Sundays is a growing trend to save time and eat healthier during the week.
Farmer's markets are popular for buying fresh, local produce.
The 'MyPlate' model replaced the food pyramid - it shows how to fill your plate with healthy foods.
